parts: Imagine owning a tiny slice of a building in Bengaluru.
Not the whole thing. Just five hundred rupees' worth.
Big assets come in big pieces, and buying them means paperwork, middlemen, and days of waiting.
Ownership of a real asset is recorded on a blockchain, as digital tokens.
Each token is a share of the real thing.
A building, a government bond, gold, even art.
Because it lives on a shared ledger, ownership can be split into small pieces,
and settled in minutes instead of days.
More than ten billion dollars of US Treasury bonds have been tokenized.
But a token is only as good as the promise behind it.
Someone still has to hold the real asset, and the law has to recognise your claim.
Tokenization doesn't make things more valuable.
It makes ownership easier to divide, move and verify.
So, that slice of a building in Bengaluru?
One day, it could be just a tap away.
